138	## 4. Architecture decisions
139	
140	**Variation axis = discriminated union (data contract) + declarative config table (layout).**
141	`typescript.md` mandates the union, and the ACs require it: Wishlist alone needs `colour` + `size` + mandatory
142	`onRemove`; PLP alone needs `sizes` + `onNotifyMe`. A flat optional-everything bag lets you build a Wishlist
143	card with no remove CTA (AC violation) and a PLP card with one (design violation).
144	
145	```
146	ZimmProductCardProps = Base & (PlpVariation | HomeVariation | WishlistVariation)
147	  base:       id, href, name, headingLevel, primaryImage, hoverImage?, images?,
148	              currentPrice?, originalPrice?, isUnavailable?, badge?
149	  'plp':      sizes?, selectedSize?, onSizeSelect?, onAddToBag?, onNotifyMe?
150	  'home':     —
151	  'wishlist': colour, size, onRemove (required), onAddToBag?
152	```
153	
154	`'recently-viewed'` is **not** a fourth member — the AC says it behaves identically to PLP, so consumers pass
155	`variation: 'plp'`. Recorded as an assumption, not a silent choice.
156	
157	The render body must **not** `switch` on `props.variation`. Layout comes from a module-level `VARIATION_CONFIG`
158	(`showBag`, `showAttributes`, `showRemove`, `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`,
159	`hoverSwapsImage`). That is what satisfies the extensibility AC: add a union member + a config row, touch no JSX.
160	
161	**The card is fluid, not 288px.** `gridSystem.ts` has `maxWidth: 'none'`. Figma's 288/179 are widths at the
162	reference artboards. The card fills its grid cell (`width: 100%`); the image holds ratio via `aspectRatio`.
163	Grid placement belongs to SFCC-80.
164	
165	**Mobile/desktop boundary = 768px** (`breakpoints.md`, 48em) — the only confirmed foundation breakpoint between
166	the 402 and 1440 artboards, and where the grid already goes 4→8 columns. `min-width` is inclusive, so the 768
167	artboard gets the desktop card. Every hover rule is additionally gated on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`
168	so a 768px touch tablet never gets hover-only content. See OQ-5.
169	
170	**Hover is CSS-only, keyed on `:hover, :focus-within`.** No React hover state — 60 tiles re-rendering on pointer
171	move is a PLP perf defect. `:focus-within` is not optional: WCAG 2.2 AA requires the revealed size selector and
172	arrows be keyboard-reachable. All reveal selectors live in one place, the organism's recipe root part, selecting
173	descendants by the shared `data-card-slot` constants. Molecules stay hover-agnostic.
174	
175	**One link per card (stretched-link).** The card holds a bag button, arrows, size options and a remove button —
176	nesting those in an `<a>` is invalid HTML and an a11y failure. The link wraps the product name only and carries
177	a `::after { position:absolute; inset:0 }` overlay; controls get `position:relative; z-index:1`. `href` arrives
178	pre-prefixed from the page. Uses `import {Link as RouteLink} from 'react-router-dom'` per `zimmColourSwatch` —
179	there is no `overrides/app/components/link/` override, contrary to a claim in `overrideStyling.md`.
180	
181	**Reuse, don't rebuild:** `ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmIcon` (`bag`, `close`, `chevron-left`,
182	`chevron-right` all exist in `ICON_MAP`). No new icons.
183	
184	**VIC pricing is not a card concern** — precedence is the page mapper's job. Deferred to SFCC-778 (OQ-6).
185	
186	---
187	
188	## 4a. Arrows vs. indicator — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
189	
190	> *"position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows"*
191	
192	The two are **mutually exclusive**, not paired. Consequences for Steps 1 and 4:
193	
194	**Split by pointer capability, not viewport width.** The gate is
195	`@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — the same gate every other hover rule already uses:
196	
197	- **hover-capable + fine pointer** → prev/next arrow buttons, revealed on `:hover, :focus-within`. No indicator.
198	- **everything else (touch tablet, mobile)** → `ZimmSlideIndicator`, always visible. No arrows.
199	
200	Capability rather than width is what actually delivers the stated intent: the 768 artboard is a *touch* tablet,
201	and a width rule alone would give it arrows it can never hover to reveal. It also keeps this consistent with the
202	card's own hover rules rather than introducing a second, differently-keyed breakpoint. **Edge case, accepted:**
203	a desktop browser resized below 768 keeps arrows (it still has a fine pointer); a touch-screen laptop gets the
204	indicator. Both are the safe failure direction — nobody is shown a control they cannot operate.
205	
206	**Two knock-on changes to the step pass criteria:**
207	
208	1. **Step 1 — the indicator is NOT `aria-hidden` on touch.** The original criterion assumed the arrow buttons
209	   announce position, so the indicator could be hidden as duplicate. Where the indicator renders there are **no
210	   arrows**, so it becomes the only position signal — hiding it would be a 1.1.1 information loss. It needs an
211	   accessible position announcement (e.g. a visually-hidden "Image 3 of 8" live region, or `role="group"` with
212	   `aria-label`). Revised criterion: exposed and announced when it is the sole affordance.
213	2. **Step 4 — mobile image paging has no mechanism and no AC.** If the indicator shows position on touch, some
214	   touch gesture must change the image. No AC covers this; the ACs only describe desktop hover. See OQ-11.
215	
216	---
217	
218	## 4b. Touch image paging — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
219	
220	> *"scroll-snap it is"*
221	
222	Native CSS scroll-snap. The dots remain a **passive readout**, visually unchanged from Figma — no enlargement,
223	no conversion to tap targets, so no departure from the design and no WCAG 2.5.8 problem to solve.
224	
225	**Implementation shape: one scroll container on every breakpoint, not two mechanisms.**
226	
227	The image strip is always a horizontally scrollable flex container with `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` and
228	`scrollSnapAlign: 'start'` on each slide. What differs by pointer capability is only the *affordance* layered
229	over it:
230	
231	| | Mechanism | Affordance |
232	|---|---|---|
233	| hover + fine pointer | same scroll container | arrows call `scrollBy()`; no indicator |
234	| touch | same scroll container | native drag; indicator reflects position |
235	
236	One container rather than two code paths means a single source of truth for "which image is showing", the
237	arrows become progressive enhancement over something that already works, and the desktop path inherits
238	keyboard scrollability for free.
239	
240	**Active-index derivation:** prefer `IntersectionObserver` on the slides over a scroll listener — 60 tiles on a
241	PLP make a per-scroll-event listener a real perf cost, and the repo already has
242	`overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.ts` (**Tier 2 — import it, do not modify it**). The `scrollend`
243	event is an acceptable alternative. Left to the Implementer; either satisfies the pass criteria.
244	
245	**Precedent:** the base `ProductScroller`
246	(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx:79-84`) already uses
247	`scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` with `overflowX: 'scroll'`. Same technique, already proven in this codebase.
248	
249	**Accepted caveat:** swipe has no explicit affordance beyond the dots implying further content. This is the
250	universal mobile convention, and the alternative (enlarging 1px dots into 24×24 tap targets) trades an
251	invisible-but-expected gesture for a visible-but-off-design control. **Action: flag to Kiera that the mobile
252	gesture is undocumented in the design**, so it lands in the spec rather than being discovered in QA.
253	
254	**Added Step 4 pass criteria:**
255	- The slide container carries `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'`; every slide carries `scrollSnapAlign`.
256	- Arrows are rendered only under `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; the indicator only outside it; assert the
257	  two never coexist in the same DOM.
258	- Arrow activation moves the scroll position (assert `scrollBy`/`scrollTo` is called — jsdom does not lay out,
259	  so assert the call, not the resulting offset).
260	- The indicator's active index tracks the observed slide, and clamps at both ends.
261	- A single-image product renders no indicator, no arrows, and no horizontal overflow.
262	- No gesture library is added — `package.json` is untouched (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7).
263	
264	---
265	
266	## 4c. Badge — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02), and it corrects the decomposition
267	
268	Nine nodes supplied; all resolve off one parent, `40001471:20702` "Badge" (a documentation board).
269	`40001471:20682` is its cover slide, not a component.
270	
271	**There are TWO badge components, not one:**
272	
273	| Component set | Node | Variants | Size |
274	|---|---|---|---|
275	| **`Badge`** | `40001471:20752` | `State=Primary` (`…20751`) · `State=Hover` (`…20750`) | 33×15 |
276	| **`Stock Status Badge`** | `40001796:7041` | `State=Available` (`…7040`) · `State=Unavailable` (`…7039`) · `State=Low stock` (`…7038`) | 66–79×20 |
277	
278	`Stock Status Badge` appears in **no acceptance criterion**. It maps to `.docs/prd/plp.md` §3
279	("**OUT OF STOCK** shown on tile when all sizes are at or below buffer threshold" and the low-stock
280	indicator) — so the PRD requirement that had no design **does** have one. Its `Low stock` state
281	corresponds to nothing in any AC, and `plp.md` §3 places low-stock *at size level*, not on the tile.
282	
283	### Decomposition correction — three slots move from Content to Media
284	
285	Reading `Image Group / Size=Large` (`40002742:46322`, 288×432) and `Size=Small` (`40002742:46321`,
286	179×268) shows the overlays live on the **image**, not in the text block:
287	
288	| Slot | Frame | Structure | Desktop | Mobile |
289	|---|---|---|---|---|
290	| **`Tag`** (the badge) | 78×48 @ top-left | `touchContainer` 30×24 @ (24,12) → `Label` text 30×8 | ✅ | ✅ |
291	| **`Close`** (remove 'x') | 48×48 @ top-right | `touchContainer` 24×24 → `Icon` 16×16 | ✅ | ✅ |
292	| **`Carousel`** (arrows) | 288×24 @ y=204 (vertically centred) | two `touchContainer` 24×24 @ x=12 and x=252 | ✅ | **absent** |
293	| **`Slide-indicator`** | 179×1, flush to the image's bottom edge (y=267 of 268) | instance | **absent** | ✅ |
294	
295	**Consequences:**
296	
297	1. **The badge slot moves from Step 5 to Step 4.** It is `Tag`, overlaid top-left on the image — not a part
298	   of `Card-content`. Remove the `badge` part from `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`; add a `tag` part to
299	   `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`.
300	2. **The remove ('x') CTA moves from Step 5 to Step 4.** It is `Close`, top-right on the image. The plan had
301	   it in `ZimmProductCardContent` — wrong molecule. Remove `onRemove` handling from Content; it belongs in
302	   Media. The union still carries `onRemove` on the wishlist member; the organism passes it to Media.
303	3. **This makes the split cleaner, not messier:** everything overlaid on the image is Media, everything below
304	   it is Content.
305	4. **§4a and §4b are confirmed by the design itself,** not just by the verbal decision — `Size=Large` has
306	   `Carousel` and no indicator; `Size=Small` has `Slide-indicator` and no `Carousel`.
307	5. **The slide indicator is a 1px hairline flush to the image's bottom edge**, not floating dots. Step 1's
308	   recipe must not assume dot geometry.
309	
310	### Two new findings that need raising, not resolving in code
311	
312	- **🟡 The badge looks interactive, against a requirement that says it must not be.** `Tag` wraps its label in
313	  a **`touchContainer`** — this file's convention for an interactive hit area (the bag icon and both arrows use
314	  the identical wrapper) — and the `Badge` component ships a **`State=Hover`**. But SPR-16 reads
315	  "~~clickable~~ product badges" and `.docs/prd/plp.md:70` says clickable badges are *"a NEW unsigned request —
316	  not confirmed… **Do not implement**."* Two independent signals in Figma versus an explicit written
317	  prohibition. **Build it non-interactive per the requirement** (a plain element, no button, no hover rule),
318	  and raise the discrepancy — do not resolve it in code.
319	- **🔵 `Icons OLD`.** The `Carousel` arrows in the current card design instance icons named
320	  `Icons OLD` (`40003066:50796`, `40003066:50798`). Deprecated naming inside a live component. Flag to Kiera.
321	- **🔵 The card's `Tag` does not instance the `Badge` component.** `Tag`'s child is a raw `Label` text node
322	  (30×8), not an instance of `40001471:20752` (33×15). The design system has a Badge component the card
323	  doesn't use. Ask which is authoritative before styling the slot.
324	
325	### Revised Step 4 pass criteria (additions)
326	
327	- `Tag` renders top-left when `badge` is supplied, as static text with no button/hover rule (§4c's
328	  interactivity question, §4f's reinstatement) — absent from the DOM (not hidden) when omitted.

# SFCC-236 — Product Card Shared Component: Build Plan

**Generated:** 2026-09-02 · **Planner:** `zm-planner` (Opus) · **Gate:** [findings.md](./findings.md)
**STATUS: GATE PASSED — ready for `zimmerMANNBuild`.** All blocking questions resolved; Tier 2 crossing approved
by Marcel 2026-09-02. Branch not yet cut (skill rule: never create a branch unasked).
**Scope: SFCC-236 only.** SFCC-83 and SFCC-84 are held — blocked on data source, surface list, and Legal's consent ruling.

---

## 1. Goal

Build the shared Zimmermann Product Card per SFCC-236 (8 pts, Sprint 4, epic SFCC-2), designed in Figma
`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` set `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size × State × Type × Unavailable), following the
FED handbook's ui-kits atomic layering and the PR #64 / `zimmColourSwatchGroup` pattern — named-export
component reading a `Zimm*`-namespaced multipart recipe via `useMultiStyleConfig`, parts applied with
`<chakra.div __css={styles.x}>`, all values `var(--zimm-*)` with explicit media queries.

**The card is the visual layer only:** every value arrives as a prop, it owns no data fetching, and it renders
the add-to-bag / size-selection controls without wiring their behaviour (SFCC-185 / SFCC-497 / SFCC-90).

---

## 2. Scale call — one branch, seven commits, one PR

```bash
git fetch origin && git checkout -b feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component origin/develop
```

The current checkout (`feature/SFCC-91_...`) is merged and must not be built on.

**Why one branch despite ~24 files:** one component family, one Figma set, one ticket, one reviewer set
(`pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` on every file). The molecules have exactly one consumer — the organism — so
merging them separately merges dead code. Splitting would also multiply the single Tier 2 touch
(`theme/components/index.ts`) across three approval cycles for an append-only registry edit.

**Full build loop (Implementer → Tester → Scorer per step).** This is a keystone blocking eight tickets, so a
wrong prop contract propagates into eight downstream stories.

| Dropped | Why |
|---|---|
| Copy-first | Nothing to copy — no file is being overridden at a mirrored path |
| Playwright / `.feature` | No page renders this component on this branch; E2E belongs to SFCC-80/90/497 |
| Bundle-size / LCP step | Nothing imports the card yet; bundle delta is zero |
| Visual regression | Chromatic/Loki is out of budget (`testing.md` excludes it); hover fidelity is a manual Storybook check |
| Multi-region fixtures | The card takes pre-formatted strings; no locale/currency logic to vary |

**Retained, non-negotiable:** `npx tsc --noEmit` · `npm run test` · `npm run lint` · `npm run audit:tokens` ·
`cr review --light --base develop`.

## 4. Architecture decisions

**Variation axis = discriminated union (data contract) + declarative config table (layout).**
`typescript.md` mandates the union, and the ACs require it: Wishlist alone needs `colour` + `size` + mandatory
`onRemove`; PLP alone needs `sizes` + `onNotifyMe`. A flat optional-everything bag lets you build a Wishlist
card with no remove CTA (AC violation) and a PLP card with one (design violation).

```
ZimmProductCardProps = Base & (PlpVariation | HomeVariation | WishlistVariation)
  base:       id, href, name, headingLevel, primaryImage, hoverImage?, images?,
              currentPrice?, originalPrice?, isUnavailable?, badge?
  'plp':      sizes?, selectedSize?, onSizeSelect?, onAddToBag?, onNotifyMe?
  'home':     —
  'wishlist': colour, size, onRemove (required), onAddToBag?
```

`'recently-viewed'` is **not** a fourth member — the AC says it behaves identically to PLP, so consumers pass
`variation: 'plp'`. Recorded as an assumption, not a silent choice.

The render body must **not** `switch` on `props.variation`. Layout comes from a module-level `VARIATION_CONFIG`
(`showBag`, `showAttributes`, `showRemove`, `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`,
`hoverSwapsImage`). That is what satisfies the extensibility AC: add a union member + a config row, touch no JSX.

**The card is fluid, not 288px.** `gridSystem.ts` has `maxWidth: 'none'`. Figma's 288/179 are widths at the
reference artboards. The card fills its grid cell (`width: 100%`); the image holds ratio via `aspectRatio`.
Grid placement belongs to SFCC-80.

**Mobile/desktop boundary = 768px** (`breakpoints.md`, 48em) — the only confirmed foundation breakpoint between
the 402 and 1440 artboards, and where the grid already goes 4→8 columns. `min-width` is inclusive, so the 768
artboard gets the desktop card. Every hover rule is additionally gated on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`
so a 768px touch tablet never gets hover-only content. See OQ-5.

**Hover is CSS-only, keyed on `:hover, :focus-within`.** No React hover state — 60 tiles re-rendering on pointer
move is a PLP perf defect. `:focus-within` is not optional: WCAG 2.2 AA requires the revealed size selector and
arrows be keyboard-reachable. All reveal selectors live in one place, the organism's recipe root part, selecting
descendants by the shared `data-card-slot` constants. Molecules stay hover-agnostic.

**One link per card (stretched-link).** The card holds a bag button, arrows, size options and a remove button —
nesting those in an `<a>` is invalid HTML and an a11y failure. The link wraps the product name only and carries
a `::after { position:absolute; inset:0 }` overlay; controls get `position:relative; z-index:1`. `href` arrives
pre-prefixed from the page. Uses `import {Link as RouteLink} from 'react-router-dom'` per `zimmColourSwatch` —
there is no `overrides/app/components/link/` override, contrary to a claim in `overrideStyling.md`.

**Reuse, don't rebuild:** `ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmIcon` (`bag`, `close`, `chevron-left`,
`chevron-right` all exist in `ICON_MAP`). No new icons.

**VIC pricing is not a card concern** — precedence is the page mapper's job. Deferred to SFCC-778 (OQ-6).

## 4a. Arrows vs. indicator — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)

> *"position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows"*

The two are **mutually exclusive**, not paired. Consequences for Steps 1 and 4:

**Split by pointer capability, not viewport width.** The gate is
`@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — the same gate every other hover rule already uses:

- **hover-capable + fine pointer** → prev/next arrow buttons, revealed on `:hover, :focus-within`. No indicator.
- **everything else (touch tablet, mobile)** → `ZimmSlideIndicator`, always visible. No arrows.

Capability rather than width is what actually delivers the stated intent: the 768 artboard is a *touch* tablet,
and a width rule alone would give it arrows it can never hover to reveal. It also keeps this consistent with the
card's own hover rules rather than introducing a second, differently-keyed breakpoint. **Edge case, accepted:**
a desktop browser resized below 768 keeps arrows (it still has a fine pointer); a touch-screen laptop gets the
indicator. Both are the safe failure direction — nobody is shown a control they cannot operate.

**Two knock-on changes to the step pass criteria:**

1. **Step 1 — the indicator is NOT `aria-hidden` on touch.** The original criterion assumed the arrow buttons
   announce position, so the indicator could be hidden as duplicate. Where the indicator renders there are **no
   arrows**, so it becomes the only position signal — hiding it would be a 1.1.1 information loss. It needs an
   accessible position announcement (e.g. a visually-hidden "Image 3 of 8" live region, or `role="group"` with
   `aria-label`). Revised criterion: exposed and announced when it is the sole affordance.
2. **Step 4 — mobile image paging has no mechanism and no AC.** If the indicator shows position on touch, some
   touch gesture must change the image. No AC covers this; the ACs only describe desktop hover. See OQ-11.

## 4b. Touch image paging — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)

> *"scroll-snap it is"*

Native CSS scroll-snap. The dots remain a **passive readout**, visually unchanged from Figma — no enlargement,
no conversion to tap targets, so no departure from the design and no WCAG 2.5.8 problem to solve.

**Implementation shape: one scroll container on every breakpoint, not two mechanisms.**

The image strip is always a horizontally scrollable flex container with `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` and
`scrollSnapAlign: 'start'` on each slide. What differs by pointer capability is only the *affordance* layered
over it:

| | Mechanism | Affordance |
|---|---|---|
| hover + fine pointer | same scroll container | arrows call `scrollBy()`; no indicator |
| touch | same scroll container | native drag; indicator reflects position |

One container rather than two code paths means a single source of truth for "which image is showing", the
arrows become progressive enhancement over something that already works, and the desktop path inherits
keyboard scrollability for free.

**Active-index derivation:** prefer `IntersectionObserver` on the slides over a scroll listener — 60 tiles on a
PLP make a per-scroll-event listener a real perf cost, and the repo already has
`overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.ts` (**Tier 2 — import it, do not modify it**). The `scrollend`
event is an acceptable alternative. Left to the Implementer; either satisfies the pass criteria.

**Precedent:** the base `ProductScroller`
(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx:79-84`) already uses
`scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` with `overflowX: 'scroll'`. Same technique, already proven in this codebase.

**Accepted caveat:** swipe has no explicit affordance beyond the dots implying further content. This is the
universal mobile convention, and the alternative (enlarging 1px dots into 24×24 tap targets) trades an
invisible-but-expected gesture for a visible-but-off-design control. **Action: flag to Kiera that the mobile
gesture is undocumented in the design**, so it lands in the spec rather than being discovered in QA.

**Added Step 4 pass criteria:**
- The slide container carries `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'`; every slide carries `scrollSnapAlign`.
- Arrows are rendered only under `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; the indicator only outside it; assert the
  two never coexist in the same DOM.
- Arrow activation moves the scroll position (assert `scrollBy`/`scrollTo` is called — jsdom does not lay out,
  so assert the call, not the resulting offset).
- The indicator's active index tracks the observed slide, and clamps at both ends.
- A single-image product renders no indicator, no arrows, and no horizontal overflow.
- No gesture library is added — `package.json` is untouched (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7).

fix(ui-kits): replace :focus-within with :has(:focus-visible) in ZimmProductCard hover reveals (SFCC-236)

Live-browser testing surfaced a real bug in the arrows hover-gating fix
from the previous commit: hovering the card correctly revealed the
carousel arrows, but moving the mouse out did not hide them again —
they stayed visible until a click landed outside the card entirely.

Root cause: clicking an arrow button gives it real DOM focus in every
evergreen browser engine, so the recipe's `&:focus-within` reveal
stayed true after the mouse left, since focus doesn't clear on
mouseleave. The identical shared-root mechanism underlies every other
hover reveal in this recipe too (price show, price hide, the
size-selector, notify-me), so a click on a size chip or the notify-me
button would reproduce the same stuck-open symptom — confirmed and
fixed across all five occurrences, not just the carousel one that was
reported.

`:has(:focus-visible)` fixes this: it only matches when the browser's
own heuristic says a keyboard focus ring is warranted, which a
mouse-click-focused <button> never satisfies in any evergreen engine,
while genuine Tab navigation still does — so keyboard parity (the
reason a focus-based reveal exists at all) is preserved and the
mouse-click case is not. First use of :has() in this codebase; fully
covered by the project's own browserslist (iOS >= 17, Android >= 14,
last 4 ChromeAndroid versions), all past its 2022/2023 shipping
baseline.

jsdom+nwsapi quirk: a later plain .focus() call stops satisfying
:has(:focus-visible) once an earlier test in the same file has driven
a real userEvent.click()-originated focus. Fixed by switching that
assertion to a real simulated Tab keypress (`user.tab()`) instead of
an imperative .focus() call — arguably a more faithful test of
"keyboard user tabs into the card" to begin with. Verified
deterministic across repeated full-file runs.
